Simulation results show input port matching, S11, better than -10 dB and transmission parameter, S21, in the order of -0.2 dB in the passband.

articleTitle: Augmented surrogates for predictive extrapolation in electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Surrogate models are a popular solution for predictive science of complex models with restricted computational budgets. We introduce the augmented surrogate, an adaption allowing both extrapolation and cost reduction for training the surrogate, and give an illustrative example for a prediction scenario for the Helmholtz problem.

articleTitle: Near-field far-field transformations for automobile antenna measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Automobile antenna measurements become more and more important and especially near-field measurements are very attractive in terms of accuracy, reliability and usefulness. Since automobiles are commonly used on streets within cities or over land, the question of the most appropriate measurement environment for antennas on automobiles is very interesting and there is a need for appropriate near-field far-field transformation approaches. Several measurement approaches for automobile antennas are discussed, where the focus is on an integral equation based near-field far-field transformation technique, which has great flexibility and can be adapted to various measurement environments by working with appropriate Green's functions. Simulation results are shown to highlight some of the capabilities of this method.

articleTitle: Examination on a self-mixing circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a self-mixing circuit is introduced, in which, a large local oscillator (LO) signal at the input will pump the device into non-linear regime, whereas the radio frequency (RF) input signal should be connected to the output port, of which the conductance will be changed by the LO drive. Both, simulations and measurements are performed for verifying the technique used.

articleTitle: Inverted P-shaped UWB antenna with dual/tri-band-notch characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A miniaturized tri-band-notch ultrawideband (UWB) antenna is presented. The antenna element consists of a P-shaped patch with a truncated ground plane. The band-notch function is achieved by introducing three distinct L-shaped slots in the main radiator. Three notches are achieved for frequency bands, i.e., WiMAX (3.1-3.8), WLAN (5.5-6.1 GHz), and downlink X-band (7.25-7.75 GHz). The antenna system is realized on Rogers Duroid 5880 having compact dimensions of 20 × 20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Moreover, the simulated as well as measured results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Even-arm modulated arm width spiral properties
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Among Frequency Independent (FI) flush-mountable antennas the modulated arm width (MAW) spiral antenna provides the simplest architecture for measuring both polarization and direction of arrival instantaneously if frequency is known. Of interest is how the improvement in detection accuracy increases with additional arms. With additional modes, the polarization and direction of the incoming signal can be better estimated. In practical applications, this angle of arrival (AOA) capability with more channels for the MAW spiral antenna improves directional accuracy.

articleTitle: Fast computation of back scattered fields for large scanned array antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Analysis of back scattered field of a large array antenna is presented. The induced current on the ground plane is obtained employing the equivalence principle and Galerkin's Method of Moment (MoM). For fast convergence a progressive wave type of basis function is proposed. Results for the scattered field intensities are shown for three cases and it is found that a tapered excitation reduces back scattered field significantly.

articleTitle: Embedding the shooting and bouncing rays method in a hybrid solver framework
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This contribution discusses aspects of the simulation of the radar cross section (RCS) for electrically large scatterers. Such simulations are needed in the development of automotive radar systems or aerospace applications. Simulating the RCS of large scatterers is typically very demanding in terms of computer runtime and memory if performed by a full wave simulation method. An asymptotic method is much less affected by these restrictions and therefore a good choice for this kind of simulation. On the other hand, asymptotic simulations are limited to structures of moderate geometrical complexity, i.e., features with sizes much larger than the simulated wavelength. In this work a hybrid domain decomposition framework is therefore used with an asymptotic method and a full wave simulation method to leverage the advantages of both simulation types.

articleTitle: Coupled modeling and experimental investigation of RF-induced heating near ablation catheters under 1.5T MRI
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: RF-induced heating of ablation catheters under 1.5T magnetic resonance image (MRI) is studied using combined computational modeling and bench testing. The transfer function of ablation catheters are measured experimentally without simplification. A high-resolution anatomical human model was then used to simulate clinical MRI RF exposure environment. The upper limit of the temperature rise was calculated around two types of catheters, namely a single wire catheter and twin wire catheter. Four different insertion depths between 17.5 cm to 70 cm inside human body model were evaluated, simulating procedure for brain or cardiac ablation. A temperature hotspot was observed around the tip of the catheter with an estimated maximum temperature rise higher than 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C for the single lead catheter and around 94<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C for twin lead catheter, with patient landmark varying from -200 mm to 1000 mm with respect to human eye-center. Three experiments were conducted in a standard phantom to validate this coupled method and it showed a good agreement between direct measurements and predicted heating results.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of mutual transient voltages in grounding systems of offshore wind farms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The paper illustrates a numerical procedure for the computation of mutual transient overvoltages transferred among typical grounding systems of wind turbines belonging to the same wind farm. We use a hybrid approach based on the circuit theory and the Method of Moments in the frequency domain. The transient response is obtained by means of the Inverse Fourier Transform efficiently computed trough a double-exponential formula.

articleTitle: A volume integral equation solver for quantum-corrected transient analysis of scattering from plasmonic nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Quantum tunneling is observed between two nanostructures that are separated by a sub-nanometer gap. Electrons “jumping” from one structure to another create an additional current path. An auxiliary tunnel is introduced between the two structures as a support for this so that a classical electromagnetic solver can account for the effects of quantum tunneling. The dispersive permittivity of the tunnel is represented by a Drude model, whose parameters are obtained from the electron tunneling probability. The transient scattering from the connected nanostructures (i.e., nanostructures plus auxiliary tunnel) is analyzed using a time domain volume integral equation solver. Numerical results demonstrating the effect of quantum tunneling on the scattered fields are provided.

articleTitle: Metagratings: A novel paradigm for efficient wavefront control
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Metasurfaces have recently gained a lot of attention in the context of beam steering, but they are subject to fundamental limitations regarding their efficiency, that cannot be overcome unless we use active or nonlocal materials. Here we show that these limitations can be overcome if we approach the problem of beam steering from a grating perspective. We show that by using metamaterial elements as the building blocks of a periodic lattice we can achieve extreme beam steering with unitary efficiency, if these elements are designed to cancel all the diffraction orders supported by the lattice apart from the one where we want to reroute an incident wave. We call such structures metagratings, in order to highlight the two main aspects of such structures, the grating principle and the metamaterial elements forming it.

articleTitle: Challenges and opportunities in modeling and optimization of 3D optical metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Planar meta-lenses, such as the v-antenna lens, are usually designed by varying two physical parameters of the v-antenna (arm length and central angle spread) and identifying a collection of antennas to discretize a modulo 2π phase swing with high transmission amplitude. Translation of the v-antenna structure into a vertically oriented antenna in a 2-dimensional array increases the necessary design parameter space, bringing to bear additional polarization and configurational possibilities which do not exist in the planar version. This talk will outline this increase in parameter space and the challenges and opportunities it presents.

articleTitle: The novel normalized method for interference suppression at subarray level
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: As the dramatic development of the computer and digital signal process techniques, the phase array radar becomes more and more important for many different kinds of military applications. In order to survive in the complicated electromagnetic environment with different kinds of interference, the adaptive digital beamformin is adopted to suppress the interference. In addition, the signal processing is performed at the subarray level in order to save the hardware resource cost. However, the sidelobe power of the antenna pattern dramatically increases since the output power of the noise for each subarray is different. In order to solve this issue, the normalized adaptive method is proposed to maintain the same output power for each subarray. The float round-off error is also analysed for the proposed method. The simulation results show that the proposed method has good performance.

articleTitle: A novel port extraction technique for coupling circuits with full wave time domain integral equation solvers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Fully coupled transient analysis of electromagnetic-circuit systems is highly desirable for a number of applications. Over the last decade or so, there have been several papers that present effective solutions to this problem within the context of full-wave differential or integral equation solvers. The method typically espoused is as follows: discretize the underlying electromagnetic (EM) system, couple with the circuit subsystem self-consistently, and then solve the coupled system. Within this framework, non-linearities are easily accounted for in the solution process. This is in direct contrast to frequency domain analysis, wherein one defines ports that couple the electromagnetic and circuit subsystems, i.e., representation of the EM system using an effective impedance. This approach permits: (a) solution only at the circuit level, and (b) one can readily incorporate different circuits without having to solve the coupled system repeatedly. In this paper, we present a technique that helps realize the same efficiency in the time domain. We will prescribe the means to effectively represent the EM subsystem in terms of a transient admittance, thus facilitating a solution to the coupled system via a circuit-level solve. Several results are presented that serve to validate the proposed approach and demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Co-simulation of a reactor assisted by microwaves
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the design and analysis of a chemical reactor assisted by microwaves is presented. A co-simulation that links the electromagnetic and thermal phenomena presented in the reactor is performed to obtain the power density and temperature distributions. The results show that a matching network is required to obtain a maximum transfer of power.

articleTitle: CT eccentricity error evaluation model based on the actual magnetization curve
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In view of the importance of the accuracy of current transformers (CTs) for monitoring and protection, a mathematical model based on actual magnetization curve is presented to predict the error caused by the eccentricity of the primary conductor. It is shown that the eccentricity will result in asymmetric magnetic field distribution and causes an error in the measurement result. In addition, the model predicted results are compared to corresponding two-dimensional transient finite element model results for verification.

articleTitle: Time-domain magnetic shielding effectiveness of planar stratified shields
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The shielding effectiveness of a planar multilayered screen is computed in the time domain in the presence of near-field magnetic sources. The proposed numerical method involves the efficient evaluation of classical Sommerfeld integrals and the inverse-Fourier transform through double-exponential formulas. For sufficiently thin screens with highly-conductive properties, an analytical method, based on a modified Cagniard-de Hoop approach, is also presented to validate the results.

articleTitle: A multiphysics time-dependent model of dielectric breakdown in solids
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A time-dependent model of dielectric breakdown in solids is presented wherein electro-quasi-statics, adiabatic heating, and peridynamics are coupled. First, the time dependent electro-quasi-static approximation is used to solve for the electrostatic potential and a nonlinear, electric-field- and temperature-dependent conductivity is used. The electric field is coupled to both the temperature (through Joule heating) and the mechanical displacement (through the Lorentz and Kelvin forces). Fracture and failure of the material are modeled using peridynamics, a non-local formulation of solid mechanics, and failure of the material may occur due to both high temperatures and high mechanical strain induced by thermal expansion. Results demonstrate several features of dielectric breakdown that are consistent with experiments.

articleTitle: Using an approximate streamline upwind/Petrov-Galerkin stabilization matrix for the solution of Maxwell's equations in dispersive materials
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The use of a full stabilization matrix in a Streamline Upwind Petrov Galerkin for the solution of Maxwell's equations when applied to dispersive materials tends to be an expensive computation. Here, an approximate diagonal-based stabilization matrix is used for dispersive material models and their solution is verified by comparing the Radar Cross Sections for two-pole Debye and Lorentz materials.

articleTitle: A tunable microstrip bandstop filter using compact spiral folded spurline for RF microwave systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper briefly describes the design principle of a tunable compact spurline bandstop filter using a spiral folded resonator. A compact rejection bandstop filter (BSF) is designed by using a conventional microstrip coupled line methodology at 2.4 GHz. The physical length has been reduced up to 75% with a good tunability results in comparing with a traditional spurline filter. Spurline section is loaded with a p-n junction varactor diode to make tunability from 1.8 GHz to 2.2GHz by applying a DC control voltage from 0V to 10V. The tunable design provides a satisfactory result for simulation and fabrication filter circuits. The modeling of the proposed filter is simulated and fabricated by Advanced Design System (ADS).

articleTitle: Design of ungrounded CPW GaN-on-Si MMICs
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This work presents a study of circuit component design in a new GaN-on-Si process being developed by the MIT Lincoln Laboratory. The process uses a thick silicon substrate with no through-vias with a multi-layer stack-up. Examples of components required for MMIC design include lines of various impedances, shorted and open stubs, tees, meander lines, and capacitors. Because the fabrication process requires the use of ungrounded CPW lines, underpasses are necessary to connect ground planes and a study of 50-Ohm lines with several underpass spacings is performed. The large range of dimensions and dielectric constants presents a challenge for full-wave simulations, and a comparison between Ansys HFSS and Sonnet Software is presented for a variety of passive circuit components implemented in the GaN-on-Si MMIC stack-up.

articleTitle: Surface integral computation for the higher order surface integral equation method of moments
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents extraction technique applied to the double higher order surface integral equation method of moments and discusses the numerical results compared with previously implemented extraction method and numerical Gauss-Legendre integration.

Author Keywords: double higher order method of moments

articleTitle: Physiologically inspired model of the skin for use in electrical impedance tomography
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A new model for the skin-electrode interface in electrical impedance tomography (EIT) is presented in which electric current is transmitted through sub-macroscopic skin features. The results of a FEM implementation are compared to measured EIT voltages collected on a human volunteer.

articleTitle: Introduction of statistical priors into the D-bar method for electrical impedance tomography
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The D-bar method is a direct (noniterative) reconstruction method for 2-D electrical impedance tomography that solves the full nonlinear inverse conductivity problem. However, the idealized model underlying the method is an obstacle to the computation of absolute images by the D-bar method. In this work, a method of correcting the data based on Bayesian techniques to better fit the idealized assumptions is proposed. Preliminary results are shown on experimental tank data.

articleTitle: Decoupled potential integral equations for electromagnetic scattering
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, an integral equation formulation will be presented in terms of decoupled scalar and vector potentials to model electromagnetic scattering from dielectric objects. The formulation can lead to several sets of integral equations with different properties; one of the sets is a second kind integral equation that doesn't result in low-frequency breakdown or dense mesh breakdown.

articleTitle: A DC to HF volume PEEC formulation based on hertz potentials and the cell method
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A new Partial Element Equivalent Circuit formulation based on Hertz potentials and the Cell Method is presented. Conductive, dielectric, and magnetic linear-homogeneous media are considered by means of conduction, polarization, and magnetization current densities. The use of edge unknowns leads to reduce system size with respect to typical face-based approaches.

articleTitle: The novel adaptive method for interference suppression
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: As the dramatic advancement in array signal processing and the computer techniques, the phase array radar becomes more and more popular. However, the electromagnetic environment is more and more complicated with different kinds of interference. The ability to suppress the interference becomes the most important consideration for the phase array radar. In this paper, the mismatch optimal detector method is proposed to suppress the interference at the subarray level. In addition, the float round-off error analysis is given. The simulation results show that the proposed method has good performance in interference suppression.

articleTitle: Spatial priors in the D-bar method for human thoracic electrical impedance tomography data
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The inclusion of a spatial prior in the high-frequency regime of the scattering transform for the 2-D D-bar method for electrical impedance tomography is studied for use with human subject data. Preliminary results on data from a human volunteer reveal improved spatial resolution when compared to a CT scan.

articleTitle: Design of broadband Luneburg lens feed manifold
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Design of broadband feed manifolds for Luneburg lenses requires intensive numerical calculations that can be time and memory consuming. This paper presents a simple and fast numerical procedure for the estimation of the field of view (FOV) coverage by a lens antenna. Details of the routine are described and the example of the lens having at least 12 dBi directivity within the FOV from 18 to 45 GHz is shown. The lens is fed by a 6×6 feed manifold made of phase center stabilized horns.

articleTitle: Spectral element boundary integral method for rapid and accurate simulations of inhomogeneous objects in layered media in nanophotonics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We recently developed an efficient numerical solver, the spectral element boundary integral (SEBI) method with the periodic layered medium dyadic Green's functions, to perform rapid and accurate simulations in nanophotonic applications. The problem is Bloch (Floquet) periodic in the lateral directions but has a multilayer background medium in the vertical direction, and arbitrary objects are embedded in the layered medium. We employ the periodic layered medium dyadic Green's function, and the surface integral equations as the radiation boundary condition to truncate the top and bottom computation boundaries of the interior domain that is simulated by the spectral element method. Therefore, all multiple scatterings within the top and bottom layered media have been analytically accounted for in the radiation boundary condition, and the computational domain is only limited to the inhomogeneous objects embedded in the layered medium. Consequently, this SEBI solver can be much more efficient than conventional methods. We demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of this solver for several typical nanophotonic applications.

articleTitle: Full-wave modeling of RF exciters using WIPL-D: Road to real-time simulation and optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Computational tools for full-wave three-dimensional (3-D) simulations of linear passive electromagnetic (EM) components have reached a point where they became both practical and necessary in computer aided design (CAD) of RF devices. Although circuit-based solvers still offer unprecedented speed and true real-time tuning, full-wave software tools, which take into account almost all physical EM phenomena, rapidly approach similar efficiency and applicability. This, however, is not possible by just using modern hardware environment, but it also requires the numerical method of choice, encapsulated within a software tool, to be extremely precise and conservative in consumption of computer resources, i.e., CPU and memory. We here report a case study which demonstrates highly efficient utilization of higher order large-domain method of moments (MoM) modeling and optimization using WIPL-D. The example includes an RF exciter, based on axial-mode helical antennas mounted on a dielectric support, designed for utilization in the state-of-the-art pre-clinical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners.

articleTitle: Sparse direct matrix solvers of finite element discretizations in electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The paper outlines some direct solution strategies for sparse matrices arising from the finite element (FE) discretization of electromagnetic (EM) models, and explores whether the conventional thinking followed by highly optimized direct method tools for sparse matrices is indeed the best available option for directly solving FEM problems in EM. Factorization memory and time, solution time, parallelization potential, and error will be considered in the comparisons between approaches. Drawing from advances in the area of integral equation (IE) methods that rely on relatively small but dense matrices, we will conjecture that direct solvers that minimize factorization fill-in while maintaining sparsity may not lead to the best overall strategy after all. We present an direct solution algorithm for FEM, based on domain decomposition that generates and operates on a lesser sparse matrix with block-wise sparse pattern, thus bridging the gap between the two extreme matrix structures, (a large fully sparse encountered in FEM and a smaller fully dense encountered in IE methods). Early results on 3D arbitrary tetrahedron meshes and arbitrary volumetric geometries suggest that the proposed approach significantly outperform state-of-the-art sparse matrix direct solvers in terms of memory while maintaining competitive run times for serial implementations.

articleTitle: The adaptive interference suppression method based on householder at subarray level
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: As the phase array meets the complicated with different kind of interference, it is very important to improve the interference suppression performance of the phase array radar. In this paper, we propose a novel adaptive method for the interference suppression for phase array radar at the subarray level. In addition, the analysis for float round-off error is also given. The simulation results show the proposed method has good performance.

articleTitle: An adaptive factorization method for inverse scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: To drastically speed up Kirsch's factorization method for inverse scattering problems, we propose a novel adaptive algorithm that automatically generates nonuniform sampling points according to the shape of the obstacle. Built upon adaptive quadrature rules, our algorithm approximates the integral of an indicator function and yields reliable reconstructions significantly faster than the standard factorization method. Numerical tests are performed to validate the effectiveness of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Design optimization of novel compact circular polarization antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The paper describes a structure and a design optimization procedure of a miniaturized circular polarization antenna with elliptical ground plane slots and feed line with stepped-impedance stubs. Constrained optimization of all antenna parameters is executed in order to explicitly reduce the antenna size while maintaining required impedance axial ratio bandwidth of 5 GHz to 7 GHz at the same time. The size of the optimized antenna is only 16.2 mm × 16.7 mm (footprint of 271 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). At the same time, the electrical and field properties of the structure are competitive for state-of-the-art designs as indicated by the comparison provided in the paper.

articleTitle: Numerical validation of a boundary element method with E and E/N as the boundary unknowns
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We recently developed a surface integral equation method where the electric field and its normal derivative are chosen as the boundary unknowns. After reviewing this formulation, we present preliminary numerical calculations that show good agreement with the known results. These calculations are encouraging and invite the further development of the numerical solution.

articleTitle: Whistler mode wave numerical raytracing in a finite temperature anisotropic plasma medium
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Whistler mode waves, which exist in a magnetized plasma, are prevalent in the Earth's magnetosphere in the extremely low frequency (ELF) and very low frequency (VLF) bands (100 Hz-30 kHz). Due to the impact of whistler mode waves on space weather processes, it is important to accurately predict the propagation trajectory of these waves. Numerical raytracing determines the power flow path of the whistler mode waves in the anisotropic medium of the magnetosphere. In the majority of previous work, magnetospheric raytracing has been implemented assuming a cold background plasma (0 K). However, a more accurate description of the magnetospheric plasma includes a background temperature of about 1 eV (11600 K). We present raytracing solutions which include the effects of finite electron and ion temperatures on the wave refractive index. The finite temperature effects are also introduced into the formulations for linear cyclotron resonance wave growth and Landau damping, which are the primary mechanisms for whistler mode amplification and attenuation in the magnetosphere. Finite temperature effects of the background plasma are shown to be most significant for highly oblique wave normal angles where the refractive index is bounded to smaller values than in the ideal cold plasma approximation.

articleTitle: Scattering analysis of silver nanoparticles for solar cell applications using integral equations
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Plasmonic nanoparticles (NPs) can be used to improve the efficiency of solar cells. Analysis of electromagnetic scattering from NPs is often carried out under the assumptions that they reside in air and have “ideal” shapes (sphere, cube, etc.) However, in a realistic setup, nanoparticles are fabricated on a substrate and their shape and size cannot be controlled precisely. In this work, a surface integral equation solver is used to accurately characterize the scattering from a realistic system, where silver hemispheres of varying sizes are fabricated on an indium tin-oxide substrate. Results obtained by the solver are compared to the experimental results obtained for a similar system.

articleTitle: A huygens surface source model for field prediction valid from sub-ELF to high frequencies
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A broad-band Huygens surface method to predict fields having knowledge of only the near magnetic field (no derivatives) on an arbitrary shaped closed boundary is presented. The proposed approach applies an augmented-integral equation formulation to calculate the electric field on the Huygens surface. The method is accurate and stable down to DC for arbitrary shaped Huygens surfaces. The proposed formulation is discretized using a locally corrected Nyström (LCN) method.

Author Keywords: locally corrected Nyström method surface integral equations

articleTitle: Size-reduced patch-antenna feedpoint parametric study
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Size-reduction techniques are applied to a circular UHF patch antenna, by introducing slits into the patch structure. The optimum slit dimensions are determined to maximize the amount of antenna-size reduction. A parametric study of the probe-feed location versus slit dimensions determines the optimum location for the probe feed location, in order to achieve matched input impedance for different slit lengths.

articleTitle: Approaches for magnetic sources reconstruction in controlled thermo-nuclear fusion technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The estimation of the unknown magnetic sources in Fusion devices by external measurements is a critical task due to its impact on several actions, including the assessment of the magnetic diagnostic system. Suitably treating the modelling of ferromagnetic materials, a linear model can be used also in presence of iron, based on the use of equivalent magnetizing currents. The several available numerical approaches provide quite different solutions while all preserving a good representation capability.

articleTitle: Nonlinear FDTD modeling of ionospheric cross-modulation experiments
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the details of a new plasma finite difference time domain (FDTD) model and demonstrate its performance characteristics. As opposed to recursive convolution or Z-transform methods, the presented method uses a direct integration method, and additionally applies the bilinear transform in the time-domain to ensure stability. The FDTD is expanded to include nonlinear terms so that the model can be used to analyze ionospheric HF heating experiments performeda at the High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program (HAARP) Observatory. We present our initial results.

articleTitle: Versatile nanoparticle manipulation with designer thermoplasmonic metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The intrinsic loss in plasmonic systems has generally been considered to be detrimental for several device applications. Using this loss to advantage, we report thermoplasmonic metasurfaces for unprecedented control over nanoparticle manipulation and assembly. We report parallel assembly of quantum emitters on plasmonic nanoantennas, stand-off manipulation of particles, and size dependent arrangement of nanoparticles. Our platform opens up vistas of applications in structural material production, quantum photonics, and color printing.

articleTitle: Perturbation approach to shape reconstruction in a rectangular waveguide using experimental data
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We consider the inverse problem of reconstructing the shape of a deformation in one of the broad walls of a rectangular waveguide. Assuming a small deformation, resulting in weak scattering, the direct problem is solved using a first order perturbation approach. Hence, the inverse problem becomes linear and is formulated as an equation system for a set of expansion coefficients. The illposedness of the inverse problem is handled with regularization, by adding a penalty term which weight is determined by the L-curve method. The theory is tested on experimental reflection data, using the dominant mode of the waveguide. The reconstructed shape is in qualitative agreement with the true shape, but a detailed resolution cannot be obtained due to insufficient quality of the experimental data. Extensions and improvements of the method are discussed.

articleTitle: Terahertz evanescent wave tunneling in bianisotropic thin films
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical investigation of electromagnetic wave tunneling through bianisotropic-bianisotropic interfaces. The dispersion relation and the conditions for terahertz evanescent wave tunneling in bianisotropic thin films are derived. The developed Berreman's matrix model is used to acquire the evanescent field characteristics through the bianisotropic layers. Fields incident with frequencies belong to the structure spectral interval will be tunneled effectively to the other side of the bianisotropic thin film via evanescent waves.

articleTitle: Late-time instability in finite difference modeling of very-low-frequency propagation in the earth-ionosphere waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) modeling is used to simulate electromagnetic wave propagation for frequencies up to 500 kHz in the waveguide formed by the Earth and lower ionosphere. Methods to solve Maxwell's equations in the magnetized plasma of the lower ionosphere are investigated and compared for their accuracy and stability. In particular, two methods are compared for long distance propagation (2000 km or longer), assessing accuracy and stability; we denote these the Lee & Kalluri method and the Boris method. The methods are compared in the presence of an absorbing boundary condition (ABC) just above the lower ionosphere. We find that both methods show late-time instabilities for certain magnetic field configurations when the ABC is used. Overall the Boris method is modestly more stable than the Lee & Kalluri method, though the two show similar stability characteristics.

articleTitle: The constitutive effective parameters of two-dimensional multilayered dielectric grating slab
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The 2D regular lattice of multilayered dielectric resonant inclusions made from different dielectric and/or magnetic material embedded in the slab is considered in this paper. An equivalent magneto-dielectric slab is found using the first-principles homogeneous theory for extracting the effective permittivity and permeability. Example is presented to study the relationship between the physical parameters of multilayered dielectric inclusions arranged in 2D lattice and their effective parameters. This study can be used as a tool for designing metamaterials with negative permittivity and/or permeability using multilayered dielectric grating slab.

articleTitle: Roof shaped rectangular slotted patch antenna at 18.3 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact sized, high frequency microstrip patch antenna with probe feeding. The patch of the antenna is pentagonal shaped which has a rectangular slot in the upper-center. Main contribution of the paper is to perturbe the side edges of the patch and to add a rectangular slot. Parametric study of those two-substrade change was investigated. The proposed structures were simulated by using the Sonnet Suites, a planar 3D electromagnetic simulation software which gave S11 value of −14.12 dB and gain value of 6.33 dB at 18.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Coupling electron transport with maxwell equations for modelling optically tunable photonic elements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Numerical approach to modelling optically controlled photonic devices is presented. The model is based on a self-consistent solution of electron and hole transport equations, semiconductor Bloch equations and Maxwell equations.

articleTitle: A novel compact microstrip bandstop filter (BSF) using spurline & stepped-impedance resonator (SIR)
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel microstrip design to increase the bandwidth of spurline bandstop filter (BSF). This design combines between conventional spurline section and stepped impedance resonator (SIR) in one filter. The compact structure of bandstop filter is designed by using microstrip transmission lines at 2.4 GHz. The proposed filter has a better and wider bandwidth with S21 from 2.1 GHz to 2.64 GHz at -20 dB rejection band while the conventional spurline has a bandwidth from 2.3 GHz to 2.4 GHz. The performance of the proposed filter is simulated by Agilent ADS with a good rejection band at -80 dB.

articleTitle: Circuit-based model order reduction for EM-CAD
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, we focus on obtaining an accurate and reliable physical-based description of the Electromagnetics we are dealing with in order to carry out a fast and accurate computer-aided design. Appropriate Finite Element solution to time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in the frequency band of interest is involved and a reliable reduced-order model is obtained. Then, the electromagnetic behavior in the microwave device is rearranged and described in terms of circuit theory, giving rise to the coupling matrix representation of the original Maxwell problem.

articleTitle: On the conforming combination of the electric and magnetic field integral equations
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A scheme to conformingly combine the electric and magnetic field integral equations (EFIE and MFIE) is presented. Particularly the range space of the method of moments (MoM) matrix system for the mixed discretized MFIE is projected to the range space of the classically discretized EFIE and then combined with EFIE. As a result, an accurate, interior resonance free, and ideally combination factor independent matrix system for the combined field integral equation (CFIE) is obtained. Numerical examples that demonstrate the accuracy and combination factor dependence are presented.

articleTitle: On synthetic aperture radar simulations using WIPL-D Pro
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper a design of a generic simulation environment for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) applications based on WIPL-D Pro solver, is presented. We discuss the measurement scenario, simulation requirements and the computing complexity in terms of time consumption and hardware resources. An example of a generation of a SAR image of a fighter aircraft, based on its full-wave monostatic RCS simulations in a frequency range between 2 GHz and 3 GHz, is presented.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave electromagnetic metasurfaces based on perforated dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A Huygens' unit cell configuration based on perforated dielectrics is proposed and demonstrated using full-wave simulations. The proposed unit cell consists of a high permittivity dielectric resonator surrounded by a honey-comb lattice. The Honey comb structure provides mechanical integrity to the unit cell, thereby enabling the unit cell scaling to mm-wave frequency bands. Two different designs are shown to demonstrate diversity of transmission characteristics achievable through the proposed cells.

articleTitle: Designing experiments to reduce uncertainty in point source locations in the Helmholtz equation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We show how a recently developed approach to formulating and solving stochastic inverse problems can be combined with an expected information gain to determine the physical placement of sensors that optimally reduce the uncertainty in the point source location for the inhomogeneous Helmholtz equation.
